taste:
The main appeal is the contrast between crisp, salty batter and moist, flaky cod. A light golden coating gives the freshly fried fillet its crunch, while the thick white fish inside stays tender. This is a substantial serving rather than a small fish portion, with the delicate flavour of the cod set against the more assertive batter.

A generous heap of thick-cut chips makes the plate feel hearty. You can choose traditional mushy peas or sweet garden peas, depending on which accompaniment you prefer. The combination suits someone looking for familiar British pub food, with texture coming chiefly from the crisp coating and the flakes of fish beneath it.
